design_lessons: Review-guided artifacts win when they translate review insights into concrete method details (e.g., specific preference pair types, named optimization objectives, specific dataset domains) rather than just rephrasing the abstract.

When review insights are generic ('clarity needs improvement', 'well-motivated'), the review-guided artifact tends to produce only cosmetic differences from the baseline, yielding ties rather than wins.

Baseline artifacts can outperform review-guided ones when the review insights cause the artifact to become vaguer or more abstract, losing specific technical anchors present in the original title/abstract framing.
claim_boundary: Across these six papers, both artifact types consistently under-specify core algorithmic mechanisms, evaluation metrics, and baseline comparisons. Review-guided artifacts provide genuine improvements primarily when review snippets contain specific technical critiques (missing algorithmic details, specific dataset gaps, concrete methodological weaknesses) that can be directly incorporated. When review snippets are high-level or evaluative ('well-written', 'needs clarity'), the review-guided artifact gains no substantive advantage. Neither artifact type adequately addresses the gap between stated contributions and the experimental evidence needed to support them, and both tend toward safe, hedged claim boundaries that do not distinguish strong from weak contributions.
